meta_description: Lorenzo Giovanni Vecchio is a full-stack software developer in Milan. Web systems, developer tools, infrastructure, and a public register of everything he builds.
meta_og_alt: Lorenzo Vecchio — engineering plates for software systems
hero_lead: I build web systems, developer tools, and the infrastructure underneath them. Currently at PwC Italy, permanently curious about the layer below.
about_title: A builder, not a slide deck.
about_intro: I like systems that are easy to operate and interfaces that do not make people think.
about_p1: I am a full-stack software developer based in Milan. I build web systems for enterprise clients at PwC Italy, and spend the rest of my time on the lower layers: Go services, Rust experiments, developer tools, and a home lab that refuses to stay boring.
about_p2: I started at ITS Angelo Rizzoli, where I studied software architecture, then worked across React front ends, Spring Boot services, and real-time applications at Nexid and ALTEN. These days I care about clear boundaries, boring infrastructure, and software that is simple to change.
about_p3: Outside the terminal I ride motorcycles, ski whenever the season allows, and train most days. I also run a server of my own: Docker Swarm, a handful of services, and a private VPN. It is where I break things on purpose.
lab_body: One server, Docker Swarm, a set of services and a private VPN. A permanent excuse to learn how systems fail — and how to bring them back.
toolkit_intro: The technologies I reach for, grouped by the layer they belong to. No percentages, no badges — just the tools.
toolkit_now: Currently exploring: Rust, language design, local-first software.

experience_intro: Where I have worked, what I studied, and what I was actually doing.
exp_its_role: Higher technical diploma in software architecture
exp_its_desc: Software engineering, project management, and real delivery. The foundation everything else sits on.
exp_nexid_desc: Designed and built from scratch the business management system of a newly formed multinational group of motorcycle parts dealers — from the domain model and architecture to the 4D (ORDA) backend and React front end — and delivered it to production. Its core is one unified database consolidating components and spare parts across every company in the group.
exp_alten_desc: On a Spring Boot platform that provisions accounts and roles across dozens of internal applications, servers and databases for a large multinational, I built new features and owned the front end through its full modernisation — AngularJS to Angular to SvelteKit — replacing libraries that had been abandoned for years and refactoring the legacy codebase along the way. I also designed and built end to end a system for cron-scheduled and one-click rotation of privileged secrets: a SvelteKit front end and backend plus a Node.js/Express worker on a separate server, talking over Socket.IO to reach systems the application server could not touch. On both projects I owned deployment automation and the DevOps side.
exp_pwc_desc: Several client applications at once. For a large multinational I work on a risk-management platform that automates detection and assessment with a purpose-trained AI model, in Spring Boot and Angular. I also helped build the internal platform that runs a project and contract from first opportunity through approval to work-progress (SAL) tracking, in Spring Boot and Next.js, and a CMDB for a major television company in Apache Causeway. I am now on a contract-first modernisation for a banking group, with OpenAPI contracts across the backend, a BFF layer and the front end.
field_intro: The parts of life that keep the rest of it in balance.
field_moto_body: Mountain roads, long weekends, and the occasional wrong turn that turns out to be the point.
field_ski_body: Skis, altitude, first tracks. The fastest way I know to reset my head.
field_sport_body: Wind, water, and a tiller in hand. The other way to clear my head.
contact_body: I am always open to a good conversation about systems, products, or the next thing worth learning. The fastest way to reach me is email.

privacy_intro: This site is built to be fast, quiet, and respectful of the people using it. No advertising, no tracking pixels, no cookie banners.
privacy_h1: What this site does not do
privacy_no_cookies: This site does not set any cookies. There is no advertising, profiling, or cross-site tracking, and no cookie banner because there is nothing to consent to.
privacy_local_storage: Your theme choice is stored locally in your browser so the page opens in the right mode. It never leaves your device.
privacy_analytics: I use Umami, a privacy-first, open-source analytics tool hosted at analytics.lorenzovecchio.dev. It records page views and basic usage data so I can understand which pages are useful.
privacy_analytics_li1: No personally identifiable information is collected.
privacy_analytics_li2: IP addresses are not stored. They are used only to derive coarse country-level information and then discarded.
privacy_analytics_li3: You are not followed across other websites or devices.
privacy_data: Analytics data is used only to improve this site. It is never sold, and it is not shared with third parties for marketing or advertising.
privacy_legal: Anonymous analytics are processed on the basis of legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR): improving the site without processing personal data or affecting your fundamental rights.
privacy_rights: Because no individual identifiers are stored, I cannot retrieve, export, or delete data about a specific visitor — there is no way to know which data belongs to you. You can still contact me with any question about these practices.
